purpose: Strict physical specimen/material axis.
examples: blood; urine; pus; cerebrospinal fluid; manure

purpose: Sampling context when physical material is unspecified or supplemental.
Preparation or processing state.
Device used to collect a specimen.
Method used to obtain the specimen.

examples: microbial isolate; cell culture; mixed culture; single cell

purpose: Sequence-derived or computational data product, not a biological sample entity.
Host-derived anatomical material distinct from anatomical part/site.
examples: stool; mucus; saliva; pus; blood; CSF

purpose: Anatomical part of a confirmed host.

Care setting or facility context.
Vital status, separate from health state and disease outcome.

Stage/phase of disease rather than disease identity.
Disease outcome when explicit.
Exposure/contact context independent of study group.
examples: household contact; close contact; exposure/contact context

purpose: Production, husbandry, or rearing context.
examples: specific pathogen free; broiler; dairy cow; farmed
